cim: Super Smash Bros. creator speaks out about the impact of artificial intelligence on the industry
cim_eredeti: Super Smash Bros. creator speaks out about the impact of artificial intelligence on the industry
szoveg_eredeti:
Renowned Japanese game designer Masahiro Sakurai, the brainchild of the Super Smash Bros. and Kirby series, shared his concerns about the widespread adoption of artificial intelligence in game development. He believes the widespread use of generative technologies could lead to a wave of unoriginal and repetitive projects. The developer noted the rapid increase in the volume of content released in recent years. While around 275 games were released on Steam annually in 2010, today that number exceeds 19,000, which will create even greater pressure on the market with the widespread adoption of AI.

Sakurai emphasizes that while modern algorithms can indeed assemble and generate working game systems, they are fundamentally incapable of creating anything truly original. True originality in game development, according to the expert, lies in the ability to offer players an experience they previously didn't even know they needed. Artificial intelligence relies exclusively on existing databases, so it can only combine or copy patterns, not make conceptual breakthroughs.

As a clear example, Sakurai cited game designer Fumito Ueda, creator of the iconic ICO and Shadow of the Colossus. An algorithm could easily analyze the visuals and mechanics of these projects to produce a similar imitation. However, AI would never be able to predict the unique vision Ueda would implement in his next work. This is the key difference between human vision and automated code generation.
